claim: CodeRabbit is configured via a .coderabbit.yaml supporting path_filters (glob include/exclude), path_instructions mapping globs to custom guidance, code_guidelines scanning convention files, learnings.scope (local/global/auto), and pre_merge_checks with off/warning/error enforcement levels.
quote: Pre-merge Checks (pre_merge_checks): Define enforcement levels per check—"off" (disabled), "warning" (notification only), or "error" (blocks merging if request-changes workflow enabled).

claim: CodeRabbit learnings.scope can be local (repo), global (org), or auto (local for public repos, global for private), and a profile setting toggles chill vs assertive review verbosity.
quote: Learnings Scope (learnings.scope): Three options control where preferences are stored—local (repository-specific), global (organization-wide), or "auto" (local for public repos, global for private ones).

claim: A safer CI pattern grants the review agent only contents:read and pull-requests:write, generates patches as files that are never auto-applied, and uses trust-tier rollout where low-risk repos auto-publish validated comments while high-risk repos restrict the agent to draft summaries needing human approval.
quote: Trust-tier rollout: Repositories are classified by risk level, with low-risk repos allowing auto-published comments after validation, while high-risk repos restrict the agent to draft summaries requiring human approval.

claim: Cloudflare's production AI review uses a bias-toward-approval model: single warnings yield approved_with_comments, only critical/production-risk patterns trigger requested_changes blocks, with a break-glass override used in 0.6% of cases.
quote: Single warnings in otherwise clean code receive approved_with_comments rather than blocks. Only critical items or patterns suggesting production risk trigger merge blocks via requested_changes.

claim: Cloudflare deploys up to seven specialized reviewer agents (security, quality, performance, documentation, compliance, release management, AGENTS.md) plus a coordinator agent that deduplicates, re-categorizes, and filters speculative findings via source-code verification.
quote: A coordinator agent performs judgment pass operations: Deduplicates findings across reviewers, Re-categorizes issues to appropriate sections, Filters speculative findings and false positives using source code verification.

claim: Over 30 days across 48,095 merge requests Cloudflare's system completed 131,246 reviews with a median review time of 3m39s, averaging $1.19 per review and 1.2 findings per review, with risk-tiered model configs costing $0.20 for typo fixes vs $1.68 for full reviews.
quote: Over 30 days across 48,095 merge requests: 131,246 total reviews completed... Average cost: $1.19 per review... typo fixes cost $0.20 vs. full reviews at $1.68.

claim: Noise reduction at Cloudflare relies on diff filtering (removing lock files, vendored and minified code), prompts with explicit 'What NOT to Flag' sections, and respecting prior human resolutions so engineers can reply 'won't fix' or 'I disagree' and retain final approval authority.
quote: Diff filtering removes lock files, vendored code, minified assets. Prompt engineering emphasizes "What NOT to Flag" sections... Engineers can reply "won't fix" or "I disagree" to AI findings.

claim: Severity-based quality gates define thresholds per category (Critical/High/Medium/Low) for new vs overall code, exiting non-zero to block merges when critical issues exceed zero, and can run alongside SonarQube as independent required status checks.
quote: A simple custom implementation filters findings by severity and exits with a non-zero code when critical issues exceed zero or high-severity issues exceed a configured threshold, blocking the merge.

claim: Semgrep's auto-triage handles roughly 60% of incoming security triage automatically with Memories enabled while maintaining 96% agreement with security researchers on true positives, and a 'not a bug' feedback button routes false positives to teams for rule tuning since the noisiest five rules cause most false positives.
quote: Semgrep's auto-triage system handles approximately 60% of incoming security triage work automatically when Memories are enabled, while maintaining 96% agreement with security researchers on true positive identification.

claim: A typical AI code review costs $0.03-$0.06 (up to $0.10-$0.20 for large PRs or rich prompts), and model routing classifies request difficulty for ~$0.001/request, saving roughly 50% of model cost by sending simple tasks to cheaper models like Sonnet and reserving Opus for architectural decisions.
quote: Model routing classifies requests by difficulty and routes them to appropriate models at a cost of approximately $0.001 per request, saving roughly 50% of model costs if half of tasks are simple.
